scope: One canonical host library instance shares capture admission across recording resources, chunk streams, runner journals and temporary ZIP output. Mixed ESM/CommonJS facades share the instance; independent JavaScript worker isolates have separate allowances.

Reserve bytes and file slots before filesystem writes or queued attachment copies. Temporary duplicates and both journal streams count while they coexist. Rejected queue/file admission returns reservations for work that never started.

Transferred manifests keep their original storage credit after writer, recording and test retirement. Failed removal or unconfirmed handle closure keeps that credit; successor tests cannot reclaim it by starting a new recording.

Failed source and private resource-reader closes retain their exact handles and prevent further admission. Disposal retries the same handles before deleting original files. ZIP input uses explicit bounded reads; assembled manifests keep their original input leases while reader closure remains uncertain.

Temporary ZIP output reserves its complete encoded size before opening. Definitive successful rename transfers output ownership; cancellation after rename dispatch retains the original completion obligation.
Earlier ingest/export failures survive secondary cleanup failures. Existing per-resource, recording, chunk, journal and final-archive limits remain in force.
verification: All 57 groups preserve frozen source and compiled identities. Nineteen storage controls per runtime cover competing recordings, duplicate cleanup, failed file closes, reader leases, late disposal, shared queues, journal finalization and definitive rename.

Existing manual traces, resource capture, sealed archives, assembly, runner journals and finalizers, native recording controls, snapshots, filmstrips and network capture pass on Bun, Node 22 and Node 24.

Four native configurations retain complete original source, snapshot, filmstrip and response resources after context closure. Actual pinned-runner and fresh packed-consumer finalization checks preserve outcomes and timeout metadata.
Source-enabled, manual and filmstrip artifacts pass the pinned actual viewer on headless shell and full Chrome. Retained ZIP CRCs, package contents and clean external watchdog receipts were audited.

An earlier 57-group pass preceded final review. Review identified unconfirmed private-reader closure and a rejected-write reservation imbalance; targeted controls and the fresh final matrix verify both corrections.
limitations: These are host capture limits, not a bound on total JavaScript or browser RSS. Native aggregate metadata, logical per-attempt enrollment and automatic runner trace coordination remain unfinished.
Public automatic trace policies remain disabled. API request integration, manual-control collision policy and complete timeout/interruption coordination are separate gates.
The frozen host baseline includes earlier unintegrated API foundation files; this checkpoint does not accept the independently changing API implementation.
The native driver is the previously accepted binary. Latest full core remains 126 groups; this is not a fresh full-core, Linux, broad parity, performance or release acceptance.
